blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Enforcement of Fundamental Rights and statutory legal rights
Applicable across the entire territory of India

items: Article 32 vs Article 226: Supreme Court writ jurisdiction (Article 32) is limited to Fundamental Rights, whereas High Court jurisdiction (Article 226) extends to ordinary legal rights as well.
Article 40 (Organization of Village Panchayats) is a frequently asked DPSP topic in civil services prelims.
Article 368 requires special majorities for constitutional amendments and cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 14 to 18 guarantee the Right to Equality, forming the core baseline of fundamental rights.
Article 21 protects Life and Personal Liberty, while Article 21A grants the Fundamental Right to Education.
Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies through writs issued by the Supreme Court.
Article 110 explicitly defines Money Bills and the exclusive authority of the Lok Sabha Speaker regarding them.
Articles 352, 356, and 360 govern National Emergency, President's Rule, and Financial Emergency respectively.
